That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

The Office of the Provost’s catalog describes grade appeals. You need documentation; possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on wanting a higher grade are not considered. A degree’s academic record is closed after the degree is conferred. [2]

If you are an undergraduate: First, within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, write to the course instructor by email or certified letter and provide supporting documentation. Make a good-faith effort with the instructor to resolve the issue; you have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you agree on an adjustment, the instructor sends an Instructor Grade Adjustment Request and documentation to the sponsoring academic unit’s Dean for approval, then to the Registrar. If you cannot agree, send a written appeal, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to that Dean within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Dean has 15 calendar days to decide. If the Dean does not support the appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination; include your position and evidence contradicting the decision or information previously unavailable. The petition must show clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. [3]

If you are a graduate student: The first step and deadline are the same, but contact the faculty member. If you cannot agree, send a written appeal with pertinent course materials or coursework to the graduate program Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Director recommends a decision to the Dean for final approval. The catalog’s supplied procedure gives no deadline for petitioning the supervising Dean after an unfavorable Director opinion. [4]

The 20-day deadlines run from the stated events; the catalog does not give a specific calendar date for your case. [3][4]

The Office of the Provost says grade appeals are considered only with supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on needing a higher grade, or on a grade penalty for an Academic Integrity violation, will not be considered. A degree’s academic record is closed once the degree is conferred. [2]

For an undergraduate course: no later than 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter to the course instructor, with supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. If the Dean’s decision does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination; include your position and evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. [3]

For a graduate course: the first deadline is also 20 calendar days after grades are posted. Write to the faculty member by email or certified letter and provide supporting documentation. You and the faculty member have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or coursework, to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles housing accommodation requests. First, “register for affiliation” with OSS and initiate contact. For only a strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor, you do not need the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; complete a request for disability support form instead. Requests are typically reviewed by a committee. Expect a decision within twenty one (21) business days after OSS receives all requested documentation; OSS may request more information. Housing is based on availability and is not guaranteed, so submit by Residence Life’s published deadlines. OSS informs Residence Life of residents requiring specific accommodations. [1][2][4][6][7]

A grade appeal is considered only in limited circumstances and requires supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based only on needing a higher grade or on an Academic Integrity penalty will not be considered. A degree’s academic record cannot be adjusted after the degree is conferred. [2]

For an undergraduate course: within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, email or send a certified letter to the instructor explaining the appeal and providing supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If unresolved, within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference, send a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost by written statement, emailed or sent by certified letter, within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination; include your position and evidence contradicting the decision or previously unavailable information. The Provost may reject petitions without clear evidence of a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. [3]

For a graduate course, contact the faculty member in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, with supporting documentation. If unresolved, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. [4]

For first-year Ramapo students applying to join Honors in the Spring, the page gives an application window of December 1 to January 8 and requires a 3.50 GPA from the Fall semester [9]. That's stressful, but one bad grade doesn't decide everything. Talking with your professor and an advisor soon can really help.

The Office of the Provost: A grade appeal is considered only in limited circumstances and requires supporting documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information unavailable when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. [2]

For an undergraduate appeal, email or send a certified letter to the course instructor no later than 20 calendar days after grades are posted, with supporting documentation. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree and want to continue, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit that sponsored the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. If the Dean does not support your appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination; include your position and evidence contradicting the decision or information previously unavailable. [3]

For a graduate appeal, contact the faculty member in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days after grades are posted, with supporting documentation. If you cannot agree, submit a written appeal by email or certified letter, including pertinent course materials or coursework, to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. [4]

The Office of Specialized Services (OSS) handles the accommodation request. An emotional support animal may be on campus when OSS has granted an accommodation; its presence may be limited to defined campus areas and generally is not permitted in academic or recreational facilities. [2][3]

First, register with OSS and submit comprehensive disability documentation from a licensed physician, psychiatrist, psychologist, social worker, or certified learning disabilities specialist. [5] Call OSS to discuss your interest; interested students will be scheduled to meet with the OSS Director. [1] OSS’s documentation page lists a writable PDF, the Animal Documentation Form 2022. [6] Documentation must demonstrate the benefits provided by the animal, and you must be granted an accommodation permitting the animal on campus. [2]

OSS and/or the Housing Accommodation Request Committee may deny a request if it is unreasonable or insufficiently documented. Reasons include insufficient evidence, an undue financial or administrative burden, a fundamental alteration of housing policy, or a direct threat to health and safety or substantial property damage. For an animal request, the College may also ask its age and size/breed, if applicable. [4]

For housing, affiliate with OSS and submit the appropriate forms; accommodations are first-come-first-served and not guaranteed. [7] Submit requests by Residence Life’s published deadlines; a late OSS request may prevent Residence Life from meeting an approved accommodation for the requested semester. [14][15]

The Office of the Provost’s catalog says a grade appeal requires documentation. Possible grounds include a computational error, factual information not considered when the grade was posted, or an alleged College Policy violation. Appeals based on simply wanting a higher grade or an Academic Integrity sanction are not considered. A degree’s record cannot be adjusted after the degree is conferred. [2]

If you are an undergraduate, email or send a certified letter with supporting documentation to your course instructor no later than 20 calendar days after grades are posted. You and the instructor have up to 15 calendar days to reach a determination. If you cannot agree, send a written appeal, with pertinent course materials or coursework, to the Dean of the academic unit sponsoring the course within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. If the Dean does not support the appeal, you may petition the Office of the Provost in writing by email or certified letter within 20 calendar days of the Dean’s final written determination. The petition must explain your position and include evidence contradicting the Dean’s decision or information previously unavailable. The Provost may reject it unless it clearly shows a factual mistake, policy violation, or action outside the Dean’s purview. [3]

If you are a graduate student, the first deadline and process are the same, but appeal next to the sponsoring graduate program’s Director within 20 calendar days of the final determination conference. [4]

Housing & Residence Life: Submit requests no later than the published deadlines. Late OSS requests may mean Residence Life cannot meet an approved accommodation for the requested semester, and arrangements depend on availability [1][2].

Office of Specialized Services (OSS):

3. Complete an Affiliation Packet. Some requests (strobe alarm, roll-in shower, wheelchair/mobility accessible residence hall, or 1st floor) do not require the Housing Accommodation Student or Provider Request Forms; only a request for disability support form is needed [3].

OSS and, in most cases, the Housing Accommodation Request Committee review the request. You can expect a decision within twenty one (21) business days after OSS receives all requested documentation. Approved accommodations are based on availability; accessible housing is not guaranteed and is provided on a first-come-first-served basis [2][7].
